messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT: High tail latency and streaming stalls detected in inference-prod (route: /v1/generate). p99 > 2s, elevated error rate on streaming connections. Pager: sarah-nguyen.

sarah-nguyen: saw alerts from dashboards, correlating p95/p99 spike with GPU node 17 backend. Linking dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/infra/inference-prod?var=node=gnode-17

mike-cho: I’m on call, acknowledging. will pull logs.

jordan-lee: noting customer impact - CS reports from Alejandra about 3 paying tenants seeing timeouts. csm-alejandra, can you confirm which customers?
csm-alejandra: acme-inc and betaapp reported streaming stalls, gamma-analytics reported higher latencies. They said partial failures starting ~03:05 UTC.

sarah-nguyen: quick health readouts:
- p95 baseline: 120ms -> 420ms
- p99 baseline: 820ms -> 2.4s
- streaming connection reset rate +8%

ops-bot: automated note: error budget burn detected, invoking on-call escalation policy.

mike-cho: running `kubectl get pods -o wide --selector=app=inference --field-selector=spec.nodeName=gnode-17` and tailing logs 
```
# tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/inference-runtime.log | grep -i stall
2026-06-18T03:06:11Z WARN stream: stall detected, kv-cache miss spike
2026-06-18T03:07:09Z ERROR gpu: nvml ECC corrected errors increased on GPU 0
2026-06-18T03:08:22Z WARN gpu: thermal throttle detected on GPU 1 - temp=98C
```

jordan-lee: nvml output from the node: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,clocks.sm,utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv` shows temps at 96-99C and occasional throttle flags.

sarah-nguyen: that matches. ECC corrections bumped from ~2/day to 120 in past hour on gnode-17. Likely intermittent GPU hardware issues causing micro stalls and host-level backpressure.

mike-cho: trying a graceful drain of the node to see if routing off helps tail latency. `kubectl drain gnode-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

sarah-nguyen: +1 to drain, but let's avoid full cluster-wide autoscaler churn. Also prepare fallback model route. Ops note: enable model-fallback to `redwood-small-q4` for latency-sensitive routes.

ops-bot: runbook step: https://runbook.redwood/internal/gpu-hardware-degradation - step 2: isolate node, step 4: contact infra.

mike-cho: drain started. moving ~12 pods off gnode-17. current rollout: 7 left to evict.

nora: routing change applied: 12% of streaming traffic rerouted to `redwood-small-q4` in us-west-2 to reduce tail impact. Observability: p99 dropped to ~1.1s within 2 minutes.

sarah-nguyen: good. but p99 still above SLO. need to finish drain + restart runtime on gnode-17. can infra run `sudo nvme-smartctl` and check dmesg?
jordan-lee: grabbing dmesg snippet: 
```
[Jun 18 03:05:07] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID 2345, GPU 0000:65:00.0, DRM err: ECC corrected errors increased
[Jun 18 03:06:11] thermal: gpu1 throttle reason: POWER_BRAKE
```

mike-cho: drainer finished. now restarting inference-runtime on the node to see if that clears stuck streams: `ssh ops@gnode-17 sudo systemctl restart inference-runtime`

ops-bot: action logged: restart_inference_runtime by mike-cho at 03:18 UTC.

sarah-nguyen: after restart, seeing temporary drop in p99 to 700ms but then climb back to ~1.4s. suggests hardware still flaky.

mike-cho: NVML query shows persistent ECC corrections increasing even after restart. suspecting GPU 0 has progressive ECC or PCI issues. recommending we cordon node and schedule maintenance: `kubectl cordon gnode-17` and open a ticket with infra for RMA.

jordan-lee: cordon applied. evicted pods are healthy on other nodes. p99 now ~650ms for most routes; some choppy streams still for long-context sessions.

sarah-nguyen: customer impact update: notifying affected customers via CSM. @csm-alejandra please escalate to enterprise contacts and share ETA.
csm-alejandra: emailing ACME and BetaApp with mitigation steps and temporary routing. asking if they want a dedicated quota bump while we stabilize.

mike-cho: I'm starting a controlled fallback for long-stream sessions: cap session length for default model to 1024 tokens and force-stream-buffer flush every 8s to avoid long-lived KV stalls. Patch:
```
PATCH: inference-runtime: limit_stream_len=1024; stream_flush_interval=8s
```

nora: applying config change on fleet. will monitor for regressions.

ops-bot: config deploy on 24 nodes: success on 22, in progress on 2.

sarah-nguyen: while we plan RMA, move gnode-17 out of rotation permanently for now. create a maintenance window and set node status to 'hardware-investigation'.
mike-cho: created ticket INFRA-4892 with logs and NVML dumps attached. notes: repeated ECC corrections, thermal events, possible PCI interconnect. Requested hardware swap.

jordan-lee: quick retrospective notes for postmortem:
- root cause: degraded GPU node (gnode-17) exhibiting ECC corrected error bursts and thermal throttling leading to intermittent stalls and backpressure in inference runtime.
- immediate mitigations: drain & cordon node, restart runtime, enable model fallback, cap session lengths, reroute traffic.
- customer impact: brief downstream stalls and elevated p99 affecting 3 customers, no data loss.

sarah-nguyen: assigning postmortem owners: mike-cho (tech lead), jordan-lee (metrics/observability), nora (ops + config), csm-alejandra (customer comms). target: 1 business day initial triage doc.

mike-cho: handoff to night team: I will be leaving the on-call at 03:45 UTC. @nora will take primary for mitigation follow-ups.
nora: taking over on-call. I'll continue to watch dashboards and coordinate with infra for RMA.

incident-bot: NOTE: Handoff: sarah-nguyen -> nora at 03:45 UTC. Pager duty: next on-call: nora.

sarah-nguyen: closing incident channel for immediate firefight; keep thread updated with infra ticket and RMA ETA. will open formal postmortem ticket after stabilization. :white_check_mark:

csm-alejandra: customers informed, offering credits for impacted windows, capturing log bundles per request.

mike-cho: final note: follow runbook for hardware failures, check for PCI firmware updates on replacement hardware.

jordan-lee: logging this as Sev2 and scheduling postmortem in #postmortems with draft due EOD tomorrow.

nora: thanks team. keeping watch. updates will be posted here. :thumbsup:
